messages:
Anya Patel: Proposal: split trace TTLs by environment and introduce a short hot window for quick search + cold bulk for cost. Thinking: prod hot=14d, prod cold=90d, staging hot=3d, staging cold=14d, dev hot=1d, dev cold=7d.
Miles Chen: :eyes: can you sketch how this impacts queries on the console? our dashboards currently only query hot index.
Anya Patel: Console searches will need a path: default search -> hot index (fast), fallback link to cold query (async). We can show a badge "older data, slower" and surface sampling/summary instead of full spans for cold reads.
Devin O'Connor: How are we handling span exporters? If we keep raw spans for 90d in cold S3, full trace reconstruct will be expensive. Maybe we persist aggregates and parent span indices to keep trace stitching cheap.
Ivy Gomez: Agree re: indices. Suggest storing full KV for 14d on hot (Elasticsearch/ClickHouse hot tier) then offload compressed OTLP protobuf blobs to cheaper object storage with a lightweight index (trace id, timestamp, service list).
Miles Chen: What about tail-based sampling? If we sample before exporter, cold storage quality drops. We need consistent sampling policy tied to env and service criticality.
Anya Patel: Yeah — propose default sampling: prod 100% hot for errors and high-latency spans, 20% for normal traffic into hot+cold; rest only in cold if above threshold. Staging/dev default to 5% hot, 100% to cold for retention.
Devin O'Connor: Can we express this in OTEL config? Something like:
```yaml
processors:
  tail_sampling:
    decision_wait: 5s
    policies:
      - name: prod_error_policy
        type: latency
        threshold_ms: 1000
exporters:
  otlp/http: {endpoint: \"<collector>\"}
```
Then collector routes spans to hot vs cold pipelines.
Ivy Gomez: That collector routing is key. Also need per-tenant overrides for enterprise customers with longer retention SLAs. Storage tiering should be pluggable per tenant.
SRE Bot: deploy-notice: config change pushed to telemetry-collector staging at 1772100780, rollouts via canary 10% -> 25% -> 100%.
Miles Chen: Cost check — rough calc: hot (14d) ~ 0.6TB/day * 14 = ~8.4TB hot, cold (90d) additional compressed ~0.3TB/day * 90 = 27TB. Cold storage cheaper but egress/restore cost for on-demand queries could spike. Need budget guardrails and per-tenant quotas.
Anya Patel: Agreed. I'll add a quota field to tenant metadata (trace_storage_bytes_limit) and expose current usage in console. Default soft-limit + alert + hard throttle.
Devin O'Connor: UX for rollouts: add a toggle in Console (Telemetry > Retention) to preview estimate for monthly cost before applying. Also show search latency SLOs per environment.
Ivy Gomez: For compliance, we should support retention override for PII-sensitive traces — automatic purge hooks that delete from both hot index and cold blobs (and S3 object lifecycle).
Miles Chen: One more: backups and snapshotting for cold archive? If a customer requests data export (legal), we need an API to produce a tarball of trace blobs and an index. Add to roadmap.
Anya Patel: Action items: 1) I'll draft an RFC with storage layout, indices, sampling defaults, and tenant override model. 2) Devin + Ivy to prototype collector routing + index proof-of-concept. 3) Miles to model cost + quota API. 4) SRE to prepare rollout plan and throttles.
Devin O'Connor: I'll start a spike today — will drop a short thread with benchmarks.
Miles Chen: +1. Also ping finance for cost apportionment.
Ivy Gomez: FYI: legal asked about 180d retention for regulated customers — include a retention-extension opt-in flow in the RFC.
Anya Patel: Great. Will post RFC by EOD Thursday. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
SRE Bot: reminder: follow the deploy checklist when changing collector routing (health checks, metrics, kill switches).
